arxiv-2103-02119.title: Central Moment Lattice Boltzmann Method on a Rectangular Lattice Journal: Journal Name
arxiv-2103-02119.creator: Eman Yahia, Kannan N. Premnath
arxiv-2103-02119.description: Abstract Simulating inhomogeneous flows with different characteristic scales in different coordinate directions using the collide-and-stream based lattice Boltzmann methods (LBM) can be accomplished efficiently using rectangular lattice grids. We develop and investigate a new rectangular central moment LBM based on non-orthogonal moment basis and involving multiple relaxation times.

arxiv-2103-14691.creator: Chee Sheng Fong, Moinul Hossain Rahat, Shaikh Saad
arxiv-2103-14691.description: Abstract We investigate low-scale resonant leptogenesis in an S ​ U ​ ( 5 ) × 𝒯 13 SU(5)\times\mathcal{T}_{13} model where a single high energy phase in the complex Tribimaximal seesaw mixing produces the yet-to-be-observed low energy Dirac and Majorana C ​ P {CP} phases.

arxiv-2112-15540.title: Numerical Simulations of Noisy Quantum Circuits for Computational Chemistry
arxiv-2112-15540.creator: J.B.Jerimiah Wright, M.G.Meenambika Gowrishankar, D.C.Daniel Claudino, P.C.L.Phillip C. Lotshaw, T.N.Thien Nguyen, A.M.Alexander J. McCaskey, T.S.HTravis S. Humble
arxiv-2112-15540.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J.B.Jerimiah Wright, M.G.Meenambika Gowrishankar, D.C.Daniel Claudino, P.C.L.Phillip C. Lotshaw, T.N.Thien Nguyen, A.M.Alexander J. McCaskey, T.S.HTravis S. Humble. The opportunities afforded by near-term quantum computers to calculate the ground-state properties of small molecules depend on the structure of the computational ansatz as well as the errors induced by device noise. Here we investigate the behavior of these noisy quantum circuits using numerical simulations to estimate the accuracy and fidelity of the prepared quantum states relative to the ground truth obtained by conventional means.

arxiv-2203-12926.title: Multitasking Framework for Unsupervised Simple Definition Generation
arxiv-2203-12926.creator: Cunliang Kong, Yun Chen, Hengyuan Zhang, Liner Yang, Erhong Yang
arxiv-2203-12926.description: Abstract The definition generation task can help language learners by providing explanations for unfamiliar words. This task has attracted much attention in recent years. We propose a novel task of Simple Definition Generation (SDG) to help language learners and low literacy readers.

arxiv-2203-13994.title: Estimating the Ratio of Means in a Zero-inflated Poisson Mixture Model Key words: Zero-inflated Poisson mixture, ratio of means, maximum likelihood estimator, EM algorithm, information matrix, standard error, Bayes estimator, conjugate prior, empirical Bayes estimator, zero-truncated Poisson distrib
arxiv-2203-13994.creator: Michael D. Perlman
arxiv-2203-13994.description: Abstract The problem of estimating the ratio of the means of a two-component Poisson mixture model is considered, when each component is subject to zero-inflation, i.e., excess zero counts. The resulting zero-inflated Poisson mixture (ZIPM) model can be treated as a three-component Poisson mixture model with one degenerate component.

arxiv-2211-00887.title: Certified Robustness of Quantum Classifiers against Adversarial Examples through Quantum Noise
arxiv-2211-00887.creator: Jhih-Cing Huang 1 Yu-Lin Tsai 2 Chao-Han Huck Yang 3 Cheng-Fang Su 2 Chia-Mu Yu 2 Pin-Yu Chen 4 Sy-Yen Kuo 1
arxiv-2211-00887.description: Abstract Recently, quantum classifiers have been found to be vulnerable to adversarial attacks, in which quantum classifiers are deceived by imperceptible noises, leading to misclassification. In this paper, we propose the first theoretical study demonstrating that adding quantum random rotation noise can improve robustness in quantum classifiers against adversarial attacks.

arxiv-2305-02151.title: Identifying the Correlation Between Language Distance and Cross-Lingual Transfer in a Multilingual Representation Space
arxiv-2305-02151.creator: Fred Philippy, Siwen Guo, Shohreh Haddadan
arxiv-2305-02151.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fred Philippy, Siwen Guo, Shohreh Haddadan. Prior research has investigated the impact of various linguistic features on cross-lingual transfer performance. In this study, we investigate the manner in which this effect can be mapped onto the representation space. While past studies have focused on the impact on cross-lingual alignment in multilingual language models during fine-tuning, this study examines the absolute evolution of the respective language representation spaces produced by MLLMs.

arxiv-2410-21456.title: Variable structures in the stellar wind of the HMXB Vela X-1
arxiv-2410-21456.creator: L. Abalo, P. Kretschmar, F. Fürst, C. M. Diez, I. El Mellah, V. Grinberg, M. Guainazzi, S. Martínez-Núñez, A. Manousakis, R. Amato, M. Zhou, M.W. Beijersbergen
arxiv-2410-21456.description: Abstract Context. Strong stellar winds are an important feature in wind-accreting high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB) systems. Exploring their structure provides valuable insights into stellar evolution and their influence on surrounding environments. However, the long-term evolution and temporal variability of these wind structures are not fully understood. Aims.

RK has been supported by ISF grant #1083/23 and by the Alexander von
arxiv-2502-07687.creator: Imry Ziv, Nur Lan, Emmanuel Chemla, Roni Katzir
arxiv-2502-07687.description: Abstract We consider the possible role of current large language models (LLMs) in the study of human linguistic cognition. We focus on the use of such models as proxies for theories of cognition that are relatively linguistically-neutral in their representations and learning but differ from current LLMs in key ways.

arxiv-2506-18298.title: Thermalization of Quantum Many-Body Scars in Kinetically Constrained Systems
arxiv-2506-18298.creator: Jia-wei Wang, Xiang-Fa Zhou, Guang-Can Guo, Zheng-Wei Zhou
arxiv-2506-18298.description: Abstract The phenomenon of quantum many-body scars (QMBS) has been studied both theoretically and experimentally, due to its unusual violation of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH). In this paper, we extend the ETH to a new description based on the grand canonical ensemble to depict the thermal properties of QMBS models.

arxiv-2601-08219.title: A Preliminary Agentic Framework for Matrix Deflation Conference: Proceedings of the Nineteenth ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining; February 22–26, 2026; Boise, ID, USA Proceedings of the Nineteenth ACM International Conference on Web Search and Data Mining (WSDM ’26), Februar
arxiv-2601-08219.creator: Paimon Goulart, Evangelos E. Papalexakis
arxiv-2601-08219.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Paimon Goulart, Evangelos E. Papalexakis. Can a small team of agents peel a matrix apart, one rank-1 slice at a time? We propose an agentic approach to matrix deflation in which a solver Large Language Model (LLM) generates rank-1 Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) updates and a Vision Language Model (VLM) accepts or rejects each update and decides when to stop, eliminating fixed norm thresholds. Solver stability is improved through in-context learning (ICL) and types of row/column permutations that expose visually coherent structure.

pmc-10666236.creator: Lena Gerhards, Gunther Wittstock
pmc-10666236.description: Rectifying behavior of alternative electronic materials is demonstrated with layered structures of a crystalline coordination network whose mixed ionic and electronic conductivity can be manipulated by switching the redox state of coordinated transition-metal ions. The coordinated transition-metal ions can convey additional functionality such as (redox)catalysis or electrochromism.

pmc-11297624.title: Children’s screen time and psychosocial symptoms at 5 years of age – the role of parental factors
pmc-11297624.creator: Janette Niiranen, Olli Kiviruusu, Riitta Vornanen, Anneli Kylliäinen, Outi Saarenpää-Heikkilä, E. Juulia Paavonen
pmc-11297624.description: Background and objectivesElectronic media (e-media) has become a universal part of young children’s daily lives. Previous studies have found an association between increased screen time and children’s psychosocial symptoms. We investigated whether parents’ psychological distress and parenting style dimensions explain the association between children’s screen time and psychosocial symptoms.

pmc-12569227.title: Novel and less invasive biomarker assays to measure liver ATP7B in Wilson disease patients
pmc-12569227.creator: Rosanna J Jiang, Lucy Chen, Kimberly Amburgey, Danie P M La, Brodie Fischbacher, Erle M Holgersen, Lucienne Ronco, Adam J Gehring, Jordan J Feld, Kahlin Cheung-Ong
pmc-12569227.description: Novel therapies for Wilson disease (WD) will require appropriate biomarkers and clinically relevant endpoints to demonstrate therapeutic efficacy. We aimed to develop robust, minimally invasive biomarker assays to assess target engagement in future clinical trials for WD therapeutics. We conducted a single-center, sample collection biomarker study in 21 patients with WD and 6 control participants.

pmc-13156862.title: Genetic and non-genetic factors influencing phenotypic variability in neurofibromatosis type 1
pmc-13156862.creator: Patricia Bianca Clissa, Sabri Saeed Sanabani
pmc-13156862.description: Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1), an autosomal dominant genetic disorder, is characterized by extensive clinical variability, posing significant challenges for prognosis and patient management. Despite being caused by mutations in a single gene, NF1, the expressivity of the disease ranges from mild cutaneous manifestations to severe, life-threatening complications, including malignant tumors, skeletal deformities, and cognitive impairments.

pmc-13288635.title: An IRES-like cis-acting element located within the EV-A71 coding region drives translation independent of the 5′-IRES and modulates viral fitness through regulated binding of viral RNA to 3D polymerase
pmc-13288635.creator: Yifan Xing, Qi Liu, Meixian Fu, Hao Zheng, Tong Zhao, Xixi Chen, Xia Cai, Jian-Er Long
pmc-13288635.description: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is a leading cause of hand, foot, and mouth disease and is occasionally associated with severe neurological complications in young children. Previous studies of EV-A71 and related enteroviruses suggested that the virus possibly contains additional cis-acting elements (CAEs) within the major open reading frame (ORF) regulating viral protein translation.

pmc-13346524.title: Design of Nanocarriers for Kidney Targeted Delivery of Nucleic Acid Therapeutics
pmc-13346524.creator: Jun Hyuk Lee, Junku Han, Sehwan Park, Hyejung Mok
pmc-13346524.description: Driven by recent successful clinical translation, nucleic acid therapeutics are being actively investigated to expand their applications to various diseases, including renal genetic disorders. As life expectancy increases and the burden of renal diseases continues to rise, nucleic acid therapeutics are considered promising alternatives to conventional treatments.

pmc-13409407.title: Structural Entanglement from Interaction-Induced Fixed Points
pmc-13409407.creator: Yukio-Pegio Gunji, Andrei Khrennikov
pmc-13409407.description: We introduce a lattice-theoretic framework for composite information systems in which tensor-like composition and entanglement are defined without presupposing Hilbert spaces or quantum states. Starting from approximation operators induced by indiscernibility relations, we construct composite systems via interaction-dependent closure operators and characterize their fixed-point lattices.

pmc-13541088.title: Comparison of the Antimicrobial Efficacy of Sodium Hypochlorite, Silver Nanoparticles, Chitosan-Capped Silver Nanoparticles, and Chlorhexidine-Loaded Silver Nanoparticles as Endodontic Irrigants Against Enterococcus faecalis: An In Vitro Study
pmc-13541088.creator: Athulya B Mohan, Aiswarya Jayaram, Anju Prakash, Sabir Muliyar, Vivek VJ, Suraj U
pmc-13541088.description: IntroductionPersistent endodontic infections are frequently associated with Enterococcus faecalis, a microorganism capable of surviving harsh intracanal conditions and penetrating dentinal tubules. Although sodium hypochlorite remains the gold-standard irrigant, nanoparticle-based irrigants have emerged as promising alternatives due to their enhanced antimicrobial properties.
